characters.id: dc:Wonder Woman|Golden Eagle Armor Wonder Woman
characters.continuity: DC Comics Post-Crisis (New Earth) / Wonder Woman Vol 2: the golden eagle armor as worn in the Devastation arc (1999) and Our Worlds at War (2001); the design originates in the Elseworlds Kingdom Come (1996), which is a separate continuity
characters.summary: Post-Crisis Diana in the winged golden eagle armor, a full suit with eagle helmet that she dons only for especially serious fights. In Wonder Woman Vol 2 she wore it while injured in the 1999 Devastation arc and against the universe-destroying Imperiex in Our Worlds at War (2001). Her flight, speed and strength remain her own Hermes- and god-granted powers; the sources do not credit the armor's wings with flight.

techniques: Amazon close combat while fully armored (the armor marks a serious, all-out fight)

mechanisms: Full-body golden armor and eagle helmet worn over her usual kit; she put it on while injured during the Devastation arc
Bullet-deflecting bracelets and reflexes, which normally provide most of her protection

weaknesses: Not established by the cited sources (no armor-specific weakness is documented for the Vol 2 appearances)
limitations: Armor is equipment she dons only for serious fights; it is not a permanent form and its protective limits are not documented in the sources
characters.formDifferences: Adds a full gold armor suit with eagle helmet and large golden wings, worn for especially serious battles. Flight is not an armor feature in the sources: Post-Crisis Diana flies by Hermes' gift with or without it.

sources.supports: Post-Crisis Diana's flight and superhuman speed were granted by Hermes (base powers she keeps while armored).
History of the golden armor: Kingdom Come #3 (1996); mainline Wonder Woman Vol 2 #144 (1999, Devastation); worn against Imperiex in Our Worlds at War (2001); bracelets usually provide her protection.
Devastation arc (1999): she wears the armor when injured and Devastation taunts her about hiding behind it; Our Worlds at War (2001): worn to fight Imperiex.
Kingdom Come origin of the gold-winged armor 'she reserved for especially intense battles against powerful foes'.

feats.claim: Wore the golden eagle armor into battle against Imperiex, a cosmic entity that destroys and rebuilds universes
Fought on in the armor while injured during the Devastation arc

campaignTags.claim: Post-Crisis Diana flies under her own power, a gift of Hermes, so she flies with or without the armor

unknowns: Exact metallurgical composition and limits of the Golden Eagle Armor across different universe reboots
Outcomes of the armored fights against Devastation and Imperiex are not stated in the sources opened

Removed by review (not supported by the sources opened): technique: Wing slashes; technique: Aerial dive-bombing; technique: Enhanced sword and shield combat (the Hephaestus sword belongs to Kingdom Come, a separate continuity); defense: armor plating rated against heavy kinetic/energy attacks; defense: Metallic wings functioning as shields; weakness: Reduced agility in confined spaces; limitation: Armor weight and wingspan restrict movement indoors; result: Various mythological threats (unnamed); conditional: Flight via the armor's wings (her flight is innate)

characters.continuity: DC Rebirth (Prime Earth): Justice League Dark Vol 2 'Last Age of Magic' and the 2018 'The Witching Hour' crossover with Wonder Woman Vol 5 (#56-57), followed by 'The Witching War'
characters.summary: Diana as the most powerful of Hecate's Witchmarked. Marked by Hecate as a child, she carried a fraction of the goddess's magic, which lay dormant until the Upside-Down Man activated it. With it she banished that demon; Hecate later possessed her, but Diana retook her body, opened a portal for the Upside-Down Man to devour Hecate, restored the Sphere of the Gods and lost the magic.

techniques: Hecate-mark magic strong enough to banish the Upside-Down Man

mechanisms: Not established by the cited sources (no magical shield or boosted invulnerability is described for this form)

weaknesses: The Witchmark is a channel for Hecate: the goddess possessed Diana fully at Nanda Parbat, and Zatanna and Constantine's exorcism went wrong
Circe trapped her in the Collective Unconscious and took control of her body during the Witching War
limitations: The magic is a fraction of Hecate's power stored in her Witchmark: dormant until the Upside-Down Man activated it, and lost after Hecate's defeat when Circe absorbed the Witchmarked's power
Banished the Upside-Down Man only with Zatanna's guidance
characters.formDifferences: Adds the Hecate Witchmark on her forehead and the goddess's stored magic (demon banishment, portal opening) on top of her usual Amazon powers, at the cost of being a vessel Hecate and later Circe could seize.

sources.supports: Base Diana's flight: in the New 52 era she gained flight from a feather thrown by Hermes.
Hecate's mark and magic, banishing the Upside-Down Man with Zatanna, Hecate's possession and defeat via a portal Diana opened, loss of the magic, and the Witching War against Circe.
Official solicitation: Hecate activates the Witchmarked, 'And the most powerful of the Witchmarked? Wonder Woman!'

feats.claim: Banished the Upside-Down Man, an immensely powerful demon, from the world with her Witchmark magic and reversed the damage it had caused
feats.citation: Justice League Dark Vol 2 ('Last Age of Magic')

feats.claim: Opened a portal for the Upside-Down Man, who devoured Hecate
Sealed Circe inside the Collective Unconscious with Hecate's power

notableResults.citation: Justice League Dark Vol 2 ('Last Age of Magic')
notableResults.note: Banished him with Zatanna's suggestions after the creature activated her Witchmark magic
Hecate possessed Diana and seized the Sphere of the Gods; Diana regained her body and opened a portal so the Upside-Down Man devoured Hecate (with the Justice League Dark)
Circe first trapped Diana and took her body; Diana struck a deal with the Upside-Down Man and sealed Circe in the Collective Unconscious

conditional.dependsOn: The Witchmark Hecate placed on her as a child, active only after the Upside-Down Man awakened it and lost after Hecate's defeat

campaignTags.claim: Marked by Hecate as a child and bestowed with a fraction of the goddess's magical ability
Used her Witchmark magic, with Zatanna's guidance, to banish the Upside-Down Man and later to seal Circe in the Collective Unconscious
Used her power to open a portal for the Upside-Down Man, who then consumed Hecate

unknowns: Long-term mental toll of retaining fragments of Hecate's magic after the event

Removed by review (not supported by the sources opened): technique: Magical energy projections; technique: Enchanted melee strikes; defense: Magical shields; defense: Divine invulnerability amplified by mystical energy; mobility: teleport (the portals she opened were for others; the Oblivion Bar portal was Detective Chimp's); claim of reality-warping magic

characters.continuity: DC Comics Post-Crisis / Modern (New Earth era: JLA, Seven Soldiers, Identity Crisis, Zatanna 2010)
characters.summary: Zatanna Zatara, a Homo magi stage magician and Justice League mage, commands magic mainly by speaking spells backwards (writing or backwards sign language also work). Wikipedia credits her with telekinesis and flight, telepathy and memory manipulation, teleportation and dimensional travel, healing, illusions and invisibility; she mind-wiped Doctor Light and Batman in Identity Crisis.

techniques: Spells written in her own blood when she cannot speak

mechanisms: Healing spells: closed a gunshot wound to her own throat with a blood-written spell (Detective Comics #833)

weaknesses: Gagging her or restraining her mouth has incapacitated her
Can be ambushed physically before she casts: the disguised Joker shot her in the throat (Detective Comics #833)
limitations: Logomancy relies on vocal commands; when she cannot speak she must fall back on written or signed spells
Her magic can become unstable, and her power is tied to her self-confidence

sources.supports: Homo magi; backwards spellcasting; listed powers (telekinesis & flight, telepathy & memory manipulation, teleportation & dimensional travel, healing, illusions & invisibility); gagging weakness; Identity Crisis mind-wipes; fights with Amazo, Joker, Black Lantern Zatara and Zor.
Daughter of Zatara and Sindella of the Homo Magi; focuses magic by speaking spell words backward, which the page notes is not strictly necessary.

feats.claim: Magically lobotomized Doctor Light and erased Batman's memories when he tried to stop her
After her mouth was magically removed, wrote spells in her own blood to restore it
Healed a gunshot wound to her own throat with a blood-written spell

notableResults.note: Freed by Wonder Woman after her mouth was removed, she defeated Amazo using Red Tornado's soul
Shot in the throat by the disguised Joker, she healed herself and helped foil his plan
Banished her undead father's Black Lantern form, though left psychologically scarred
Recovered her lost powers, captured Gwydion and defeated the rogue Time Tailor Zor

campaignTags.claim: Homo magi with mastery of various forms of magic
Performs magic by saying phrases or spells backwards, or by writing or signing them
Her listed powers include teleportation and dimensional travel
Her listed powers include telekinesis (with flight)
Listed telepathy and memory manipulation; erased Batman's memories and mind-wiped Doctor Light in Identity Crisis

unknowns: Upper limits of her power when drawing directly from extra-dimensional magical planes without exhausting herself
Flight, healing of others and invisibility are listed by Wikipedia but no specific feat was confirmed, so natural-flight, heals-others and invisibility tags were not proposed

characters.continuity: Mainline DC Comics New Earth Hunter Zolomon as Zoom (Flash vol. 2 #197, 2003). Excludes Prime Earth, TV and other versions; Prime Earth details differ.
characters.summary: Wally West's rival, whose chronokinesis lets him change how fast time runs around him rather than drawing on the Speed Force. He was unraveled by Wally's own time manipulation.

techniques: alters the speed time flows relative to himself
speed-based attacks as a consequence of that power
offense.range: close; extends to wherever his local time field reaches (not sourced)

mechanisms: local time manipulation used evasively (inferred from power description)

notableResults.citation: Flash comics summarised on DC Database and Wikipedia mirror
notableResults.note: Wally turned time-stream manipulation against him, unraveling Zoom's timeline and reverting him to the crippled, powerless Hunter Zolomon

weaknesses: His own power can be turned against him: Wally unraveled his timeline
Powers came from a Cosmic Treadmill accident, not the Speed Force
unknowns: Whether his power is linked to the Speed Force is disputed among fans.
Top speed and area of effect not sourced.

sources.supports: New Earth: localized chronokinesis, alters time relative to himself rather than using the Speed Force; Wally reverts him using time-stream manipulation
Wikipedia mirror: most speedsters use the Speed Force, but Zolomon can alter the speed time flows around him
DCU Guide: former FBI agent; exploded Cosmic Treadmill left him with time-related abilities
Zoom is Wally West's biggest foe; powers came from a Cosmic Treadmill accident
